wal_note_from_red_team.observation: red team saw -wal mtime move between arms, concluding the DB was not zero-write
wal_note_from_red_team.measured: each replication run left journeys/travelers/journey_operations_contexts unchanged at 44/59/27 with 0 non-GET requests, while a 24,752 B -wal exists per copy
wal_note_from_red_team.reading: the WAL grows from read-time writes on GET endpoints (this product's GET /experience writes on read), not from POSTs. So 'zero write' must be stated as 'zero non-GET requests and unchanged row counts in the tables the wizard owns', not 'the DB file was untouched'.
wal_note_from_red_team.corollary_for_gates: a run-shape that reuses one DB copy across runs cannot tell reproducibility from residue; that is why the arbiter's per-run copy requirement is right, and it is applied here.
